commit_message:
add stablehlo pass to convert IR with quantized types to standard types (#24785)

On current main the test i added here fails with:

```
input_qdq.mlir:4:24: error: failed to legalize operation 'stablehlo.uniform_quantize' that was explicitly marked illegal: %0 = "stablehlo.uniform_quantize"(%arg0) : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 1.000000e-02>>
    %quantized_input = stablehlo.uniform_quantize %input : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 0.01:0>>
                       ^
input_qdq.mlir:4:24: note: see current operation: %0 = "stablehlo.uniform_quantize"(%arg0) : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 1.000000e-02>>
```

This PR adds a shlo pass to convert IR with quantized types to integer
math + standard types.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@480b2c9eb47f

Advances third_party/llvm-project from 8c5193b41f2f to 480b2c9eb47f,
no carried-over or new reverts.

One adaptation was required:

llvm/llvm-project@9e43e04108dd ("[mlir][arith] Gate min/max expansion in
arith-expand behind include-min-max (#211884)") stops arith-expand from
expanding arith.maximumf/minimumf/maxnumf/minnumf unless the new
include-min-max-f option is set. For VMVX, ArithToVM has conversion
patterns for arith.maximumf/minimumf but none for arith.maxnumf/minnumf,
so the arith.maxnumf emitted by the linalg.softmax decomposition no
longer legalized and VMVX -> VM conversion failed in tests/e2e/linalg/softmax.mlir.

Setting includeMinMaxF on the VMVX arith-expand invocation restores the
previous behavior. include-min-max-i is left off because the VM dialect
has native integer min/max ops for both i32 and i64.

LLVMCPU has direct lowerings to the llvm.intr.maximum/maxnum.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beysel@roofline.ai>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[LLVM integrate] drop carried LLVM commit reverts (#24779)

Adapt to LLVM bazel changes for config.h in musl, required by:
b8cc84591b6a [bazel] Correct config.h definitions for musl (#207295)
    
Remove per-function target attributes to re-eanble inlineing under
alwaysinline. Required by the combination of:
7bdca287b102 [InlineCost] Never inline functions with incompatible
target features (#205113)
37b8e765ce48 [AlwaysInliner] Do not inline on attribute mismatches

The changes have been assisted by Claude Code, but were manually checked
and cleaned.

commit_message:
add stablehlo pass to convert IR with quantized types to standard types (#24785)

On current main the test i added here fails with:

```
input_qdq.mlir:4:24: error: failed to legalize operation 'stablehlo.uniform_quantize' that was explicitly marked illegal: %0 = "stablehlo.uniform_quantize"(%arg0) : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 1.000000e-02>>
    %quantized_input = stablehlo.uniform_quantize %input : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 0.01:0>>
                       ^
input_qdq.mlir:4:24: note: see current operation: %0 = "stablehlo.uniform_quantize"(%arg0) : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 1.000000e-02>>
```

This PR adds a shlo pass to convert IR with quantized types to integer
math + standard types.

commit_message:
[LLVMGPU] Add NVVM paged attention pipeline test (#24770)

## Summary

Adds NVVM compile-time pipeline coverage for paged decode attention.

Part of #24766.

The test follows the existing ROCm paged-attention coverage in
`pipeline_vector_distribute_reduction_gfx942.mlir`, adapted for CUDA's
32-thread subgroups.

- Adds an NVVM `VectorDistribute` testcase covering dynamic page tables,
paged KV gathers, causal masking, and `online_attention` lowering.
- Uses an explicit CUDA layout with 128-thread workgroups and 32-thread
subgroups.

## Testing
```sh
/workspace/iree-build/tools/iree-opt --split-input-file \
  --iree-codegen-llvmgpu-nvvm-lowering-pipeline="include-llvm-lowering=false" \
  compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_vector_distribute_paged_attention.mlir \
  | /workspace/iree-build/llvm-project/bin/FileCheck \
      compiler/src/iree/compiler/Codegen/LLVMGPU/test/NVVM/pipeline_vector_distribute_paged_attention.mlir

Signed-off-by: weimin023 <tnwilly@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

commit_message:
[iree-benchmark-module] support processing outputs after benchmarking (#24789)

Add --enable_output_processing option to iree-benchmark-module to make
it process the outputs of the last benchmark iteration executed. For
example, this processing can be writing the outputs to disk. The output
processing is the same as done by iree-run-module.

In order to achieve this:
- Move output processing from run_module.c into a new process_results.c.
  - Slightly change the benchmark loop in iree-benchmark-module-main.cc:
- Use a output VM list passed by the caller and only create a
local/temporary one if none is passed.
- Move clearing of the output list from the end of the benchmark loop
body to the beginning of the benchmark loop body, so that the results of
the last benchmark iteartion are available at the end of the loop.
- Clear the results/output list after the benchmark loop if a local list
has been used. Otherwise, keep the results in the output list passed by
the caller.

Also change the main function of iree-benchmark-module:
 - Allocate an output list if output processing is enabled.
- Pass the output list (if allocated) to benchmarking loop (for now only
for synachonous execution of modules).
 - Process outputs in the output list at the end (if list is allocated).

---------

it process the outputs of the last benchmark iteration executed. For
example, this processing can be writing the outputs to disk. The output
processing is the same as done by iree-run-module.

In order to achieve this:
- Move output processing from run_module.c into a new process_results.c.
  - Slightly change the benchmark loop in iree-benchmark-module-main.cc:
- Use a output VM list passed by the caller and only create a
local/temporary one if none is passed.
- Move clearing of the output list from the end of the benchmark loop
body to the beginning of the benchmark loop body, so that the results of
the last benchmark iteartion are available at the end of the loop.
- Clear the results/output list after the benchmark loop if a local list
has been used. Otherwise, keep the results in the output list passed by
the caller.

Also change the main function of iree-benchmark-module:
 - Allocate an output list if output processing is enabled.
- Pass the output list (if allocated) to benchmarking loop (for now only
for synachonous execution of modules).
 - Process outputs in the output list at the end (if list is allocated).

commit_message:
[Preprocessing] Support quantized convolutions in channels-last conversion

Quantized convolutions (e.g. ONNX QLinearConv, lowered to
linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw_q with extra zero-point operands) were either
skipped or mis-transposed by the channels-last preprocessing passes,
which assumed a fixed (input, filter, output) operand triple.

ConvertConvToChannelsLast:
 - Generalize ConvBuilderFn to take ValueRange inputs / ArrayRef<AffineMap>
   inputMaps instead of a hardcoded input+filter pair.
 - defaultConvBuilderFn now applies the dimension permutation to every
   input map and builds the indexing map list from all operands. In the
   tiled/pack path (tiling-factor > 0), pass-through operand maps (e.g.
   zero-points) are extended to the new iteration space's dimension count,
   since their results are dimension-independent and need no remapping.
 - transposeConvLikeLinalgOp uses getDpsInputs()/getDpsInits() and
   indexingMaps.back() for the output instead of operand index 2, and
   forwards the extra (zero-point) operands untouched along with their
   original maps.

ConvertConvFilterToChannelsLast:
 - Generalize ConvertGenericFilterToFhwc to use isConvolutionInterfaceImpl
   instead of inferConvolutionDims (which bails on the extra zero-point
   operands), and to preserve all operands/indexing maps when rebuilding
   the transposed generic. One pattern and one set of guards now handles
   CHWF, CFHW, and HWCF uniformly, for both plain and quantized
   (multi-operand) convs, including grouped convs.

Adds lit test coverage for a quantized linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw_q op
(both the plain-transpose and tiled/pack paths) and for quantized
CHWF/CFHW/HWCF generics (plain and grouped), and updates an existing
conv_filter_to_channels_last.mlir test whose HWCF-layout generic was
previously left untouched (no pattern supported HWCF-layout generics at
all) and is now correctly transposed to FHWC.

Fixes #24774

commit_message:
[Preprocessing] Support quantized convolutions in channels-last conversion

Quantized convolutions (e.g. ONNX QLinearConv, lowered to
linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw_q with extra zero-point operands) were either
skipped or mis-transposed by the channels-last preprocessing passes,
which assumed a fixed (input, filter, output) operand triple.

ConvertConvToChannelsLast:
 - Generalize ConvBuilderFn to take ValueRange inputs / ArrayRef<AffineMap>
   inputMaps instead of a hardcoded input+filter pair.
 - defaultConvBuilderFn now applies the dimension permutation to every
   input map and builds the indexing map list from all operands. In the
   tiled/pack path (tiling-factor > 0), pass-through operand maps (e.g.
   zero-points) are extended to the new iteration space's dimension count,
   since their results are dimension-independent and need no remapping.
 - transposeConvLikeLinalgOp uses getDpsInputs()/getDpsInits() and
   indexingMaps.back() for the output instead of operand index 2, and
   forwards the extra (zero-point) operands untouched along with their
   original maps.

 - Generalize ConvertGenericFilterToFhwc to use isConvolutionInterfaceImpl
   instead of inferConvolutionDims (which bails on the extra zero-point
   operands), and to preserve all operands/indexing maps when rebuilding
   the transposed generic. One pattern and one set of guards now handles
   CHWF, CFHW, and HWCF uniformly, for both plain and quantized
   (multi-operand) convs, including grouped convs.

(both the plain-transpose and tiled/pack paths) and for quantized
CHWF/CFHW/HWCF generics (plain and grouped), and updates an existing
conv_filter_to_channels_last.mlir test whose HWCF-layout generic was
previously left untouched (no pattern supported HWCF-layout generics at
all) and is now correctly transposed to FHWC.

commit_message:
[Preprocessing] Support quantized convolutions in channels-last conversion

Quantized convolutions (e.g. ONNX QLinearConv, lowered to
linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw_q with extra zero-point operands) were either
skipped or mis-transposed by the channels-last preprocessing passes,
which assumed a fixed (input, filter, output) operand triple.

ConvertConvToChannelsLast:
 - Generalize ConvBuilderFn to take ValueRange inputs / ArrayRef<AffineMap>
   inputMaps instead of a hardcoded input+filter pair.
 - defaultConvBuilderFn now applies the dimension permutation to every
   input map and builds the indexing map list from all operands. In the
   tiled/pack path (tiling-factor > 0), pass-through operand maps (e.g.
   zero-points) are extended to the new iteration space's dimension count,
   since their results are dimension-independent and need no remapping.
 - transposeConvLikeLinalgOp uses getDpsInputs()/getDpsInits() and
   indexingMaps.back() for the output instead of operand index 2, and
   forwards the extra (zero-point) operands untouched along with their
   original maps.

ConvertConvFilterToChannelsLast:
 - Generalize ConvertGenericFilterToFhwc to use isConvolutionInterfaceImpl
   instead of inferConvolutionDims (which bails on the extra zero-point
   operands), and to preserve all operands/indexing maps when rebuilding
   the transposed generic. One pattern and one set of guards now handles
   CHWF, CFHW, and HWCF uniformly, for both plain and quantized
   (multi-operand) convs, including grouped convs.

Adds lit test coverage for a quantized linalg.conv_2d_nchw_fchw_q op
(both the plain-transpose and tiled/pack paths) and for quantized
CHWF/CFHW/HWCF generics (plain and grouped), and updates an existing
conv_filter_to_channels_last.mlir test whose HWCF-layout generic was
previously left untouched (no pattern supported HWCF-layout generics at
all) and is now correctly transposed to FHWC.

Fixes #24774

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@480b2c9eb47f (#24793)

Bumpy `llvm-project` from `8c5193b41f2f` to `480b2c9eb47f`, no
carried-over or new reverts.

One adaptation was required:

llvm/llvm-project@9e43e04108dd stops arith-expand from expanding
`arith.maximumf/minimumf/maxnumf/minnumf` unless the new
`include-min-max-f` option is set. For VMVX, `ArithToVM` has conversion
patterns for `arith.maximumf/minimumf` but none for
`arith.maxnumf/minnumf`, so the `arith.maxnumf` emitted by the
`linalg.softmax` decomposition no longer legalized and `VMVX -> VM`
conversion failed in `tests/e2e/linalg/softmax.mlir`.

Setting `includeMinMaxF` on the VMVX arith-expand invocation restores
the previous behavior. `include-min-max-i` is left off because the VM
dialect has native integer min/max ops for both i32 and i64.

LLVMCPU has direct lowerings to the `llvm.intr.maximum/maxnum`.

Assisted-by: Claude Code and reviewed by me.

Bumpy `llvm-project` from `8c5193b41f2f` to `480b2c9eb47f`, no

`arith.maximumf/minimumf/maxnumf/minnumf` unless the new
`include-min-max-f` option is set. For VMVX, `ArithToVM` has conversion
patterns for `arith.maximumf/minimumf` but none for

Setting `includeMinMaxF` on the VMVX arith-expand invocation restores
the previous behavior. `include-min-max-i` is left off because the VM
dialect has native integer min/max ops for both i32 and i64.

LLVMCPU has direct lowerings to the `llvm.intr.maximum/maxnum`.

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@480b2c9eb47f (#24793)

Bumpy `llvm-project` from `8c5193b41f2f` to `480b2c9eb47f`, no
carried-over or new reverts.

One adaptation was required:

llvm/llvm-project@9e43e04108dd stops arith-expand from expanding
`arith.maximumf/minimumf/maxnumf/minnumf` unless the new
`include-min-max-f` option is set. For VMVX, `ArithToVM` has conversion
patterns for `arith.maximumf/minimumf` but none for
`arith.maxnumf/minnumf`, so the `arith.maxnumf` emitted by the
`linalg.softmax` decomposition no longer legalized and `VMVX -> VM`
conversion failed in `tests/e2e/linalg/softmax.mlir`.

Setting `includeMinMaxF` on the VMVX arith-expand invocation restores
the previous behavior. `include-min-max-i` is left off because the VM
dialect has native integer min/max ops for both i32 and i64.

LLVMCPU has direct lowerings to the `llvm.intr.maximum/maxnum`.

Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@480b2c9eb47f (#24793)

Bumpy `llvm-project` from `8c5193b41f2f` to `480b2c9eb47f`, no
carried-over or new reverts.

One adaptation was required:

llvm/llvm-project@9e43e04108dd stops arith-expand from expanding
`arith.maximumf/minimumf/maxnumf/minnumf` unless the new
`include-min-max-f` option is set. For VMVX, `ArithToVM` has conversion
patterns for `arith.maximumf/minimumf` but none for
`arith.maxnumf/minnumf`, so the `arith.maxnumf` emitted by the
`linalg.softmax` decomposition no longer legalized and `VMVX -> VM`
conversion failed in `tests/e2e/linalg/softmax.mlir`.

Setting `includeMinMaxF` on the VMVX arith-expand invocation restores
the previous behavior. `include-min-max-i` is left off because the VM
dialect has native integer min/max ops for both i32 and i64.

LLVMCPU has direct lowerings to the `llvm.intr.maximum/maxnum`.

Assisted-by: Claude Code and reviewed by me.

---------

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beysel@roofline.ai>

commit_message:
add stablehlo pass to convert IR with quantized types to standard types (#24785)

On current main the test i added here fails with:

```
input_qdq.mlir:4:24: error: failed to legalize operation 'stablehlo.uniform_quantize' that was explicitly marked illegal: %0 = "stablehlo.uniform_quantize"(%arg0) : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 1.000000e-02>>
    %quantized_input = stablehlo.uniform_quantize %input : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 0.01:0>>
                       ^
input_qdq.mlir:4:24: note: see current operation: %0 = "stablehlo.uniform_quantize"(%arg0) : (tensor<1x256xf32>) -> tensor<1x256x!quant.uniform<i8:f32, 1.000000e-02>>
```

This PR adds a shlo pass to convert IR with quantized types to integer
math + standard types.

Signed-off-by: default <ziereis@roofline.ai>
